paper: Fang et al. 2018, BMC Systems Biology 12:66, DOI 10.1186/s12918-018-0587-5
topic: B2-phylogroup E. coli metabolic adaptation in IBD
verdict_context: PARTIAL REPLICATION (strong): FBA on K-12 reference + tblastn on 3 B2 references (LF82/UTI89/NRG857c) confirm central Table-1 growth phenotypes and clean operon-wide loss of frlA/B/C/D/R in B2. Full 110-strain rerun and 53-IBD-isolate per-strain GEMs not done.

open_questions.q: Is B2-phylogroup metabolic-pathway divergence from commensal phylogroups (A, B1) dominated by loss events (like the frl operon in this paper) or by gain events (island acquisitions, HGT), when measured across a modern 5,000+ E. coli pan-genome rather than 110 strains?
open_questions.basis: Fang et al. show a clean operon-wide LOSS of frlA/B/C/D/R in 3/3 B2 references, but their 110-strain pan-genome cannot resolve whether loss dominates the B2 metabolic signature genome-wide. BV-BRC now indexes 5,737 complete E. coli genomes (verified this pass); the loss-vs-gain balance in the B2 lineage across that expanded corpus has not been quantified. Report C3/C5 verified on 4 strains only.
open_questions.next_steps: Pull all BV-BRC B2-classified complete assemblies (Clermont in-silico or ClermonTyping-based); build a directional pan-genome (present-in-ancestor vs. absent-in-clade) using PanX or Roary at CD-HIT 80%; tabulate metabolic KEGG modules with LOSS-signature (present in A/B1, absent in B2 majority) vs. GAIN-signature (absent A/B1, present B2 majority); test the null that loss and gain contribute equally to phylogroup differentiation.

open_questions.q: Does colibactin (pks island, clbA-S) prevalence in IBD-derived B2 isolates correlate with the frl-loss / GalNAc-advantage metabolic signature reported by Fang et al., or are they two independent B2 markers?
open_questions.basis: The paper focuses on metabolic capability (frl loss, TBP-aldolase GalNAc advantage) but does not link its metabolic signature to the well-known IBD-relevant colibactin/pks island of B2 strains. LF82, UTI89, and NRG857c all carry pks; whether the metabolic and genotoxic B2 traits are linked (shared regulatory or physiological origin) vs. independently acquired is unresolved. This replication tested metabolic markers only.
open_questions.next_steps: For every B2 isolate in a reannotated corpus, co-score (a) frl-operon presence/absence via tblastn, (b) pks-island presence via clbA/clbS tblastn + island synteny check, (c) GalNAc TBP-aldolase (agaA/S/Y) copy count. Test 2x2 contingency (frl-loss vs. pks-present) on IBD vs. non-IBD B2 cohorts; if independent, they carry orthogonal diagnostic information for IBD-associated B2 typing.

open_questions.q: When a per-strain GEM is reconstructed for each of the 53 IBD isolates (not done in this replication) and simulated in a mucin-representative gut-lumen medium rather than defined M9, do B2 GEMs show a quantitative fitness advantage that survives realistic uptake-flux constraints, cross-feeding, and oxygen limitation?
open_questions.basis: This replication ran FBA on K-12 reference iML1515/iJO1366 in defined M9 with one carbon at 10 mmol gDW-1 h-1 and reproduced Table-1 qualitative growth (6/8 exact, 2 within paper variance). The paper's central in-vivo claim - that B2 metabolic capability drives mucosal colonization - requires per-strain B2 GEMs under gut-representative constraints, which was not done in either the paper (which used FBA in a defined aerobic medium) or this replication.
open_questions.next_steps: Reconstruct GEMs for the 53 IBD isolates via CarveMe or KBase; define a mucin-representative medium (mucin-derived glycans at physiological ratios, low O2 tension, host-secreted amino acids, secondary bile acids); run pFBA or dynamic FBA per strain; report growth-rate distributions per phylogroup rather than per-substrate binary calls. Compare against defined M9 baseline to see if B2 advantage survives realistic constraints.

open_questions.q: Do adherent-invasive E. coli (AIEC) pathotype markers - which are typically defined by adhesion/invasion phenotype (FimH variants, LPF, LEE-negative) - track independently of the Fang et al. B2 metabolic signature, or is the AIEC phenotype partly a downstream consequence of the frl-loss / GalNAc-utilization metabolic profile?
open_questions.basis: LF82 and NRG857c are both canonical AIEC references and both B2, and both show the operon-wide frl loss verified here. The paper argues metabolic capability enables colonization, and AIEC by definition can colonize/invade IEC-line monolayers. Whether AIEC-classified strains are a metabolically distinguishable subset of B2 (beyond the paper's phylogroup-level treatment) is not addressed by Fang et al. or by this replication.
open_questions.next_steps: Assemble a curated AIEC-vs-non-AIEC B2 corpus (annotated by adhesion/invasion assay in original publications); rerun frl-operon presence, TBP-aldolase copy count, mucus-glycan gene panel, and FBA-predicted GalNAc/mucin growth per strain; test whether AIEC B2 strains cluster metabolically apart from non-AIEC B2 strains, and whether metabolic markers alone can predict AIEC classification with meaningful sensitivity/specificity.

open_questions.q: Does within-host E. coli evolution across IBD flare vs. remission episodes select for further loss of Amadori-product / rare-sugar catabolism (as suggested by the frl-loss signature) or does it select for gain of stress-response and cross-feeding genes, and does the direction of selection differ by phylogroup?
open_questions.basis: Fang et al.'s design is cross-sectional (53 IBD isolates from separate patients), not longitudinal. The paper's frl-loss claim is a phylogroup-level static observation, not a within-host trajectory. Whether the metabolic signature deepens (further catabolic loss) or shifts (regulatory/stress gain) under repeated IBD-flare inflammation is unresolved. This replication is also fully cross-sectional.
open_questions.next_steps: Design or reanalyze a longitudinal IBD cohort with sequential E. coli isolates from the same patient across flare/remission cycles; pan-genome each patient-series separately; test for enrichment of (i) additional metabolic-gene loss vs. (ii) stress/regulatory-gene gain per phylogroup lineage; contrast B2 lineages against A/B1 lineages in the same patients to test whether B2 shows a distinct trajectory. Deposit results with per-strain accessions to enable others to layer per-strain GEMs (extending the Fang et al. approach into a time axis).
